minutes.headline: Committee heard FY15 technology and school budget requests; no budget vote taken, after a superintendent report on the football cancellations.

The committee set a March budget-input target for a new tolerance and diversity advisory committee and heard the building reuse recommendations.

what_happened.line: The School Committee took no votes and made no decision on the FY15 budget; it heard requests from technology and three schools.
The committee agreed to ask a new tolerance and diversity advisory committee for a budget ballpark in March and to finish by the end of the school year.
The superintendent reported on the investigations and the cancelled football games, an informational item with no vote.
Technology's line falls because laptop purchases moved to the capital plan, and a network administrator position is planned.
Principals of the primary school, Turkey Hill and the high school explained requested increases, including restoring cut supply lines at Turkey Hill.

why_it_matters: These requests are the first stage of the FY15 school budget, so they shape the school portion of the town budget, mostly taxes, that residents vote on later.
Moving laptop purchases to the capital plan lowers the technology operating line but shifts that cost to a different part of town spending.
watch_next: The next agenda, which is to carry a conditional vote on turning over TCP to the town.
March, when the tolerance and diversity advisory committee is to be asked for a budget ballpark.
